faqs.a:
(a)
Notice generally.
Whenever, as authorized in this article, a member of the police department or public
               works designee impounds and/or tows a vehicle and the member or other designee knows
               or is able to ascertain from the registration the name and address of the registered
               owner thereof, the member shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, give or cause
               to be given notice in writing to such registered owner of the impounding and towing,
               the reason(s) for the impounding and towing, and the place to which the vehicle has
               been towed, if applicable. If the vehicle was towed to a lot maintained by a city-designated
               tow contractor, a copy of the notice shall be forwarded to the tow contractor.
(1)
Exceptions:
(i)
If a vehicle is impounded because it contains evidence or is otherwise of evidentiary
               value, notice to the owner shall be made pursuant to applicable court orders and statutes.
               Notification related to the disposition of any such vehicle, or property contained
               within such vehicle, shall be made pursuant to article III, abandoned, lost, or unclaimed
               property and evidence of
chapter 62
, offenses, of this Code.
(ii)
If, due to fire, flood, snow or other storm, or other disaster or emergency, a vehicle
               is towed a very short distance to the nearest place of safety and not to an impound
               facility, notice to the owner may be made in any reasonable manner and within a reasonable
               period of time in light of the disaster or emergency circumstances.
(b)
Contents of written notice.
The written notice may contain all towing and impoundment information deemed reasonable
               and necessary by the police department and shall also contain the following statement:
"A member of the Arvada Police Department (APD) or other designee has ordered the
               impoundment, towing, or removal of this vehicle for the reason(s) set forth herein.
If you feel that the impoundment of this vehicle was improper, you have ten (10) calendar
               days from the date of this notice to file a written request with the Arvada city manager's
               office, City of Arvada, 8101 Ralston Road, Arvada, CO 80001-8101 for a hearing regarding
               the propriety of this impoundment. Such hearing should be scheduled within seven calendar
               days of the date your written request is received by the city manager's office. Your
               written request should contain a telephone number at which you may be reached during
               the day.
FAILURE TO REQUEST A HEARING WITHIN TEN CALENDAR DAYS OF THE DATE OF THIS NOTICE SHALL
               BE DEEMED A WAIVER OF YOUR RIGHT TO A HEARING.
At the conclusion of the hearing, the hearing officer will decide two issues: whether
               you have the right to possess the vehicle, and whether there was authority to impound
               or remove (meaning impound and tow) the vehicle. The hearing officer shall be authorized
               to waive the impound and/or towing and storage fees if the hearing officer finds that
               there was no reason to believe that legal authority for the impound or removal of
               the vehicle existed.
THE APD SUGGESTS THAT YOU RETRIEVE YOUR VEHICLE FROM IMPOUNDMENT AS SOON AS POSSIBLE
               TO MINIMIZE THE ACCRUAL OF STORAGE FEES. The retrieval of your vehicle from impoundment
               does not waive your right to a subsequent hearing and reimbursement of towing and
               storage fees.
If you do not claim the vehicle and pay all applicable fees and costs within 30 calendar
               days of the date of the impoundment, the vehicle will be sold."
(c)
Service of written notice to the registered owner.
(1)
The written notice shall be deposited in the United States mail no later than 72 hours
               (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and city holidays) after the impoundment of the vehicle.
               In lieu of mailing, the written notice may be personally served upon the owner of
               the vehicle by any member of the police department.
(2)
If the vehicle is not registered in Colorado, or if the license plate or vehicle identification
               number is expired, altered, or missing, the police department shall send the notice
               required by this section as soon as is reasonably practicable, without regard for
               the 72-hour limit set forth in subsection (1).
(d)
Request for hearing.
A request for hearing shall be filed with the city manager's office on a form prescribed
               by the city. The request shall be in writing, and shall be filed within ten calendar
               days of the date of the written notice to the registered owner above. Failure of the
               registered owner to request a hearing within ten calendar days shall be deemed a waiver
               of the right to such hearing.
(e)
Hearing officer.
(1)
The city manager, or designee thereof, shall appoint a hearing officer for the purpose
               of conducting hearings on the impounding and towing of vehicles.
(2)
Except as otherwise set forth herein, the hearing officer shall have the authority
               to conduct tow hearings as set forth in division 3, Administrative hearings, of article
               V, administrative policies, procedures and rule making and hearings, of chapter 2,
               administration, of the Arvada City Code. Except as otherwise set forth herein, tow
               hearings shall be conducted as set forth in said division 3 of article V of chapter
               2 of the Arvada City Code.
(3)
The hearing officer may assess administrative costs and fees for services required
               to process and conduct tow hearings. Any such costs and fees shall be set pursuant
               to
section 2-261
(a) of this Code. The city may require said costs and fees be paid upon application
               for a tow hearing; a portion or all of the costs and fees may be refunded at the conclusion
               of the hearing should the person requesting the hearing be deemed the owner of the
               vehicle and should the hearing find there was no legal authority for the impoundment
               and/or tow. Failure to pay the required costs or fees upon application for a tow hearing
               shall be deemed a waiver of the right to a hearing.
(f)
Hearing.
(1)
If the owner of a vehicle files a written request for a hearing as set forth herein,
               a hearing shall be conducted before the hearing officer. Such hearing should, to the
               extent reasonable, be conducted within seven calendar days of the city's receipt of
               the written request for the hearing, unless the vehicle owner waives, in writing,
               the opportunity for a speedy hearing. Notice of a hearing may be served to the owner
               and to witnesses in any reasonable manner, including electronically, as may be determined
               by the hearing officer to be reasonable under the circumstances. The only two issues
               to be resolved by the hearing officer shall be whether the person requesting the hearing
               has the right to possession of the vehicle and whether there was authority to impound
               or remove the vehicle. In this subsection, the phrase "authority to remove" shall
               mean facts that would lead a person of ordinary care and prudence to believe that
               the person who impounded or removed the vehicle, or who caused it to be impounded
               or removed, had the legal authority to do so.
(2)
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Code, a tow hearing shall be conducted
               in an informal manner, and the hearing officer shall not be bound by technical rules
               of evidence. Failure of the registered owner to attend a scheduled post-seizure hearing
               shall be deemed a waiver of the right to such hearing. The person requesting the hearing
               shall have the burden of proving that he or she is the registered owner of, or otherwise
               entitled to possess the vehicle. The city shall have the burden of proving that there
               was authority to impound the vehicle. The burden of proof shall be by a preponderance
               of the evidence. The decision of the hearing officer shall be a final agency decision.
a.
The hearing officer may issue a decision verbally at the conclusion of the hearing
               or may issue a written decision following the hearing. In all cases, the decision
               shall be dated. A written decision may be served upon the parties in any reasonable
               manner, including electronically.
(3)
Only upon findings by the hearing officer that the person requesting the hearing has
               the right to possession of the vehicle, and that the person who impounded or removed
               the vehicle or caused it be impounded or removed did not have the legal authority
               to impound the vehicle, may the hearing officer order the city to either fully or
               partially reimburse the owner of the impounded vehicle for towing and storage fees
               and costs paid by the owner or to pay all or part of accrued fees and costs to the
               towing and storage company.
Exception:
In any case where the hearing officer finds that a vehicle impoundment and/or tow
               was authorized, but where he also determines that there exists clear and convincing
               evidence that the documentation on which the impoundment and/or tow was based was
               incorrect, he may authorize the release of the vehicle in accordance with any rules
               or requirements for release set by the city-designated tow contractor and may authorize
               the payment by the city to the tow contractor all towing and storage fees. The chief
               of police or designee thereof may also determine by clear and convincing evidence
               that the documentation on which the impoundment and/or tow was based was incorrect
               and may authorize the release of the vehicle and payment of fees as set forth herein.
               Should the chief or his designee make such determination after a dispute is filed,
               the chief or his designee shall notify the hearing officer of such determination,
               and the hearing officer shall vacate the pending hearing and refund any administrative
               fees and costs already paid.
(4)
Any finding by the hearing officer that the person requesting the hearing has the
               right to possession of the vehicle shall be binding only upon the parties to the hearing
               and not upon any third party or governmental entity.
(g)
Disposal.
Disposal of vehicles that have been impounded and towed by, or by order of, a member
               of the police department shall be disposed of in accordance with state or city law,
               police department rules and procedures, or the contract with the city-designated tow
               contractor, as may be applicable.
(h)
Applicability.
The hearing and reimbursement provision contained in subsection (e) of this section
               shall only apply to vehicles that have been impounded by, or caused to have been impounded
               by, a member of the police department or other authorized designee.
(i)
Compliance with time requirements.
The time periods placed upon the city in this section are directory in nature. Failure
               of the city to strictly comply with the time periods set forth in this article shall
               not cause an automatic forfeiture of the city's rights under this Code.
(j)
Appeal.
Any final agency decision rendered pursuant to this provision may be appealed as
               set forth in Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 106(a)(4).
